items.title: Wheels in lockfile are not filtered by `exclude-newer`
items.reason: Closest structural analogue: uv respected a per-file eligibility condition during resolution but serialized ineligible wheels into `uv.lock`. Its trigger is upload time rather than yank status.

items.title: Omit wheels from lockfile based on `--exclude-newer`
items.reason: Introduced the implicated `PrioritizedDist::built_dist` filtering path. Its `is_excluded` predicate covers only `ExcludeNewer`, providing a direct implementation and test precedent.

items.title: Reduce repeated information across `File` in a single distribution
items.reason: Its discussion explicitly recognizes that PEP 592 yank status is per-file. It tracks metadata deduplication, not this lockfile correctness defect.

items.title: Resolve from lockfile cannot detect yanked versions
items.reason: Establishes that an existing lockfile cannot discover later yank state without querying the registry. The new report instead concerns a yank already known during fresh lock generation.

items.title: Filter out yanked files
items.reason: Historical fix establishing per-file yank filtering in the older `pip-compile` path. It did not cover universal `uv.lock` artifact aggregation.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests. Literal searches covered `yanked wheel` with `uv.lock`, per-file and partial yanks, PEP 592, `data-yanked`, `AllowedYanks`, and `is_excluded`. Conceptual searches covered mixed yank state on private indexes, artifact eligibility versus version selection, and frozen lock behavior. Fix-oriented searches followed historical yank filtering and the analogous `exclude-newer` lockfile fix. astral-sh/uv#19112 was inspected but ruled out because it requests rechecking a whole version yanked after locking; astral-sh/uv#17143 concerns incorrect hash selection rather than artifact filtering.

type_reason: Source confirms that fresh resolution marks a non-allowed yanked file incompatible per file, but `PrioritizedDist::built_dist` filters only `ExcludeNewer` incompatibilities. The yanked wheel is therefore serialized with its URL and hash, while lockfile deserialization has no yank metadata. Retaining a known-unusable artifact when an unyanked alternative exists is incorrect behavior, and no existing item tracks this exact partial-yank gap.
summary: No duplicate was found. astral-sh/uv#12296 and astral-sh/uv#12299 are the closest structural precedent; astral-sh/uv#6145, astral-sh/uv#5928, and astral-sh/uv#413 establish the surrounding per-file yank and lockfile behavior.
draft_response: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. The current source confirms a lockfile filtering gap for partial yanks, and I couldn’t find an existing issue tracking this exact case. This is analogous to astral-sh/uv#12296, fixed by astral-sh/uv#12299 for `--exclude-newer`: `PrioritizedDist::built_dist` filters artifacts through `is_excluded`, but that predicate currently covers `ExcludeNewer` and not `Yanked`. The next step is a focused `uv lock` integration regression test with one yanked and one unyanked wheel for the same version, followed by a fix that preserves the existing cases where a yanked artifact is explicitly allowed.
